en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eleventh Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Knowledge is Dissociated from Consciousness: Is knowledge dissociated from consciousness?
Yes, it is.
Is form (rūpa) Nibbāna? Is the eye-base …pe… the tangible-object-base Nibbāna?
One should not say so …pe… Is knowledge dissociated from consciousness? One should not say so.
“Yes.

“Is wisdom (paññā), the faculty of wisdom (paññindriya), the power of wisdom (paññābala), right view (sammādiṭṭhi), and the investigation-of-dharmas factor of enlightenment (dhammavicayasambojjhaṅga) dissociated from consciousness (cittavippayutta)?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].

Is wisdom (paññā), the faculty of wisdom (paññindriya), the power of wisdom (paññābala), right view (sammādiṭṭhi), and the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment (dhammavicayasambojjhaṅga) associated with consciousness (cittasampayutta)?
Yes. Is knowledge (ñāṇa) associated with consciousness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is knowledge dissociated from consciousness? Yes.
To which aggregate does it belong?
It belongs to the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha). Is the aggregate of mental formations dissociated from consciousness (cittavippayutta)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the aggregate of mental formations dissociated from consciousness? Yes.
Is the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception dissociated from consciousness?
One should not say so …pe… Is knowledge included within the aggregate of mental formations dissociated from consciousness?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is wisdom included within the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and dissociated from consciousness?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is wisdom included in the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and associated with consciousness?
Yes. Is knowledge included in the aggregate of mental formations and associated with consciousness?

It should not be said so … [as before] … Knowledge is included in the aggregate of mental formations and is dissociated from consciousness; wisdom is included in the aggregate of mental formations and is associated with consciousness? Yes.
Is one part of the aggregate of mental formations associated with consciousness and one part dissociated from consciousness?
It should not be said so … [and so on] … Is one part of the aggregate of mental formations associated with consciousness and one part dissociated from consciousness?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception partly associated with consciousness and partly dissociated from consciousness?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is it not to be said that knowledge is dissociated from consciousness?
Yes, it is.
Should an Arahant who possesses eye-consciousness be called "one possessing knowledge"?
Yes. Is that knowledge associated with that consciousness?
It should not be stated thus.
For if that were so, would it then follow that knowledge is dissociated from consciousness?
And would an Arahant who possesses eye-consciousness be called "possessed of wisdom"?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is wisdom associated with that consciousness?
You should not say so.
Therefore, wisdom is dissociated from consciousness.
The discussion on the end of knowledge being dissociated from consciousness is finished.
